incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Taiwan Company Act (Company Act), Articles 1, 6, 9, 128, 129, 130, 148, 153, 156, 161-1, 171, 178, 192, 203, 208, 218, 266, 267, 274, and 387, together with the Act Governing Electronic Payment Institutions, Articles 3, 4, 6, 9, 10, and 33, and the authorization and administration regulations issued by the Taiwan Financial Supervisory Commission (FSC).

incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Company Registration Application Form under Article 387 of the Taiwan Company Act, together with the Articles of Incorporation, executed First Board Resolution, capital verification certificate, FSC establishment permission, director consents, and local agent authorization.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Under the Taiwan Company Act, there is no mandatory minimum paid-in capital for a limited liability company as a general matter. However, because the entity is an Electronic Money Institution (EMI) under ISIC 6619, the FSC imposes a special minimum paid-in capital requirement for licensed EMI operations, currently fixed at NT$100 million or such higher amount as the FSC prescribes in the establishment permission. This capital must be fully subscribed and fully paid in cash before the FSC operating license is granted. The funds must be placed in a blocked escrow account at a Taiwan bank approved by the FSC, and no portion may be released or withdrawn without the prior written consent of the FSC. A Taiwan-licensed certified public accountant must issue a capital verification report, and the escrow certificate and verification report must accompany the MOEA registration filing.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS RESOLUTION OF [CN__TW__CN_JV_LTD] (THE COMPANY), A LIMITED LIABILITY COMPANY TO BE INCORPORATED UNDER THE TAIWAN COMPANY ACT, ADOPTED BY UNANIMOUS WRITTEN CONSENT OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS ON [DATE]. WHEREAS THE COMPANY HAS BEEN FORMED AS A SINO-FOREIGN EQUITY JOINT VENTURE FOR THE LAWFUL CONDUCT OF ELECTRONIC MONEY INSTITUTION ACTIVITIES UNDER ISIC 6619, INCLUDING VIRTUAL IBAN ISSUANCE, DIGITAL WALLET RESERVE MANAGEMENT, AND RELATED CARD-LINKED AND ACCOUNT-LINKED PAYMENT SERVICES; WHEREAS THE BOARD HAS REVIEWED THE DRAFT ARTICLES OF INCORPORATION, THE FSC ESTABLISHMENT PERMISSION, THE SHARE SUBSCRIPTION AND CAPITAL ESCROW SCHEDULE, THE REGISTERED OFFICE LEASE, AND THE CORPORATE GOVERNANCE AND ANTI-MONEY-LAUNDERING COMPLIANCE CHARTER; AND WHEREAS THE BOARD DETERMINES THAT THE FSC LICENSING REGIME REQUIRES FULL SUBSCRIPTION AND PAYMENT OF THE MINIMUM PAID-IN CAPITAL INTO A BLOCKED ESCROW ACCOUNT PRIOR TO OPERATIONAL AUTHORIZATION. NOW THEREFORE IT IS RESOLVED THAT: ONE, THE ARTICLES OF INCORPORATION ARE ADOPTED IN THE FORM PRESENTED, AND THE CHAIRMAN AND ANY DESIGNATED SUBSCRIBER ARE AUTHORIZED TO EXECUTE, ACKNOWLEDGE, AND FILE THE SAME WITH THE MINISTRY OF ECONOMIC AFFAIRS. TWO, THE AUTHORIZED SHARE CAPITAL OF THE COMPANY SHALL BE NT$[AMOUNT], DIVIDED INTO [NUMBER] ORDINARY SHARES WITH PAR VALUE NT$[AMOUNT] EACH; ALL SHARES SHALL BE SUBSCRIBED AND FULLY PAID BY THE JOINT VENTURE SHAREHOLDERS, AND THE DIRECTORS SHALL ENSURE THAT THE FSC MINIMUM CAPITAL IS DEPOSITED INTO THE DESIGNATED ESCROW ACCOUNT AND SHALL NOT RELEASE SUCH FUNDS WITHOUT FSC PRIOR WRITTEN CONSENT. THREE, THE REGISTERED OFFICE OF THE COMPANY IS HEREBY ADOPTED AT [ADDRESS], TAIWAN, AND THE DIRECTORS ARE AUTHORIZED TO EXECUTE THE LEASE, UTILITY CONTRACTS, AND ANY AMENDMENTS NECESSARY FOR THE OFFICE TO SERVE AS THE LEGAL SEAT AND PRINCIPAL PLACE OF ADMINISTRATION. FOUR, THE BOARD AUTHORIZES THE OPENING OF THE COMPANY PRIMARY BANK ACCOUNT AND EXCLUSIVE SETTLEMENT ACCOUNT WITH [BANK NAME], AND DESIGNATES [NAME A] AND [NAME B] AS AUTHORIZED SIGNATORIES, WITH THE CORPORATE SEAL PLUS THE SIGNATURE OF ANY ONE AUTHORIZED DIRECTOR AND THE SIGNATURE OF THE COMPLIANCE OFFICER FOR HIGH-VALUE TRANSACTIONS, OR SUCH OTHER SIGNING MATRIX AS THE BOARD MAY ADOPT. FIVE, THE FOLLOWING STATUTORY OFFICERS ARE APPOINTED: [NAME A] AS CHAIRMAN AND LEGAL REPRESENTATIVE, [NAME B] AS GENERAL MANAGER, [NAME C] AS COMPLIANCE OFFICER, [NAME D] AS AML/CFT OFFICER, AND [NAME E] AS COMPANY SECRETARY, EACH WITH THE POWERS AND DUTIES PRESCRIBED BY LAW, THE ARTICLES, AND THE INTERNAL AUTHORIZATION MATRIX. SIX, THE BOARD DIRECTS THE GENERAL MANAGER AND COMPLIANCE OFFICER TO ADOPT AND MAINTAIN, BY FURTHER RESOLUTION AS REQUIRED, THE AML/CFT POLICY, KYC PROCEDURES, INFORMATION SECURITY PROGRAM, BUSINESS CONTINUITY PLAN, AND ALL GOVERNANCE INSTRUMENTS REQUIRED BY THE FSC. SEVEN, THIS RESOLUTION IS EFFECTIVE IMMEDIATELY, AND ALL REGULATORY FILINGS AND OPPORTUNE APPLICATIONS NECESSARY TO DISCHARGE THE FOREGOING AUTHORIZATIONS ARE HEREBY DELEGATED TO THE GENERAL MANAGER, COMPLIANCE OFFICER, AND COMPANY SECRETARY, ACTING JOINTLY OR SEVERALLY. PASSED AND ADOPTED BY THE UNANIMOUS CONSENT OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS ON THE DATE FIRST WRITTEN ABOVE.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Secure electronic money institution establishment permission from the Financial Supervisory Commission
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Financial Supervisory Commission, Financial Institutions Department / Banking Bureau, Taipei, Taiwan.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the EMI establishment permit application to the FSC, which is the mandatory competent regulator for electronic payment institutions before company registration. The application must include the proposed business name and scope, paid-in capital plan, detailed business plan for virtual IBAN issuance and digital wallet reserve management, AML/CFT risk assessment, KYC policies, information security framework, shareholder and ultimate beneficial owner disclosures, and board member competency information. The FSC will review the high-risk nature of the digital wallet activities and the adequacy of internal controls. The establishment permission letter will state a validity period within which incorporation, capital escrow, and MOEA registration must be completed.
required_dossiers: FSC EMI establishment application form
Detailed business plan and operating model
Proposed Articles of Incorporation
Paid-in capital schedule and escrow plan
Shareholder and ultimate beneficial owner identification documents
AML/CFT and KYC policy drafts
Information security and business continuity framework
Board member CVs and declaration forms
Financial statements of joint venture shareholders
Parent company board resolutions and powers of attorney
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the FSC issues a supplementary questions letter, respond in writing within 30 calendar days, or such longer period as FSC specifies, and provide the exact documents requested. If the establishment application is denied, the applicant may file an administrative appeal with the FSC within 30 days after receipt of the written denial, or submit a fresh corrected application once all deficiencies have been remediated.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Prepare and notarize incorporation documents and complete capital escrow verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Taiwan District Court notary or licensed Taiwan attorney-notary, and a Taiwan-licensed certified public accountant registered for company capital verification.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After FSC approval, convene the first shareholders and board meeting to adopt the Articles, appoint the first directors and the chairman, and authorize the execution of the incorporation filing. The shareholders must execute the Articles of Incorporation and Share Subscription Agreement, remit the minimum paid-in capital into a blocked escrow account at a bank acceptable to the FSC, and obtain a CPA capital verification certificate evidencing full subscription and payment. The board resolution and Articles must be notarized, and any foreign corporate shareholder documents must be authenticated by the applicable Taiwan overseas representative office or authorized notarial body before being used in Taiwan.
required_dossiers: FSC establishment permission letter
Executed Articles of Incorporation
Share Subscription Agreement
Escrow agreement and bank capital remittance proof
CPA capital verification certificate
First Board Resolution
Notarized consent letters of directors
Passports or company registration certificates of shareholders
Power of attorney appointing local authorized representative
Registered office lease agreement and landlord consent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or CPA identifies signature, translation, or certification defects, correct the relevant documents and resubmit for notarization or reissuance of the capital verification certificate. If the chosen escrow bank refuses or delays certification, select another FSC-approved bank, notify the FSC in writing, and re-document the capital deposit. The period may be extended by three additional business days for technical documentary corrections.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File company registration application with the Ministry of Economic Affairs
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Commercial Affairs, Company Registration Division, Taiwan Company Registry.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the Company Registration Application to MOEA within the validity period stated in the FSC establishment permission, together with the notarized Articles, First Board Resolution, CPA capital verification report, FSC permission letter, director and statutory officer consents, and registered office lease. MOEA will examine whether the Articles contain all mandatory Company Act content, whether the capital has been validly subscribed and paid, whether the business scope lawfully describes EMI activities, and whether the applicant has provided the required shareholder and officer identification. Upon approval, MOEA will issue the company certificate and uniform business number. The company may not commence consumer-facing EMI operations until the FSC operating license is subsequently issued.
required_dossiers: Completed Company Registration Application Form
FSC establishment permission letter
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
First Board Resolution
CPA capital verification certificate and escrow certificate
Valid identification of directors, supervisor, and legal representative
Registered office lease and landlord consent
Name and business scope pre-approval certificate
Corporate seal specimen
Proof of payment of state registration fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If MOEA issues an electronic query or inquiry regarding missing attachments or inconsistent signatures, respond and correct the filing within 15 calendar days. If the registration is rejected, the applicant may file an administrative appeal within 30 days after receipt of the rejection notice, or resubmit a corrected application without loss of the original filing priority where the correction is formal in nature.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain the FSC Electronic Payment Institution operating license
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Financial Supervisory Commission, Financial Institutions Department / Banking Bureau, Taipei, Taiwan.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After company registration, apply to the FSC for the formal Electronic Payment Institution operating license. The application must demonstrate full compliance with the Act Governing Electronic Payment Institutions, including final Articles, issued share capital certificate, escrow release approval, corporate bank settlement account confirmation, board and officer appointment records, internal control system audit reports, AML/CFT compliance manual, information security and cybersecurity certificates such as ISO 27001 or equivalent, and an independent auditor report on financial and settlement systems. The FSC may conduct an on-site inspection of the registered office and perform a technical review of the planned virtual IBAN and digital wallet systems before issuing the license. The license authorizes the company to operate as a licensed EMI under high-risk AML supervision.
required_dossiers: FSC EMI operating license application form
MOEA company registration certificate
Final notarized Articles of Incorporation
Certificate of issued and paid-in share capital
Escrow account release confirmation approved by FSC
Corporate bank and settlement account certificate
Board resolution appointing statutory officers
Internal control and internal audit reports
AML/CFT and KYC compliance manual
Information security and ISO 27001 certificate or equivalent report
Business continuity plan
Independent auditor financial and settlement system report
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the FSC requests additional information or remedial measures, submit the requested materials within 30 calendar days. If the operating license is denied, the company may petition the FSC for administrative reconsideration within 30 days and may correct deficiencies; the FSC establishment permission remains available only during its stated validity period and may be renewed only under applicable statutory conditions.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete tax, labor, municipal fire-safety, and ancillary registrations for the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Taxation Bureau of the Ministry of Finance, Bureau of Labor Insurance, and the local municipal fire safety authority for the registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the MOEA and FSC authorizations are in place, complete tax registration with the National Taxation Bureau, register for uniform invoice and electronic invoicing administration, and obtain the unified business number certificate for tax purposes. Register the company as an employer with the labor insurance, health insurance, and pension authorities before hiring staff. For the registered office, obtain a standard building occupancy certificate and fire-safety compliance inspection from the local municipal fire agency. This is not an industrial or physical licensing process because ISIC 6619 covers financial services rather than manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehousing; therefore, no Environmental Impact Assessment is required.
required_dossiers: Tax registration application form
Company registration certificate
Articles of Incorporation
Valid identification of the legal representative
Registered office lease agreement
Bank account certificate
Uniform invoice administration application
Labor, health insurance, and pension registration forms
Municipal fire-safety inspection application
Building occupancy permit or its equivalent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If tax registration is filed late, request administrative mitigation of any penalty and provide justifiable cause. If the municipal fire-safety inspection identifies deficiencies, remediate the defects and request a re-inspection. If labor insurance registration is delayed, cooperate with the Bureau of Labor Insurance to establish the effective employment date and correct all employee onboarding records before the next periodic compliance review.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable. No industrial authority licensing is required because the entity is a digital financial services provider under ISIC 6619, not a physical manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehousing operation.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable. The mandatory operating authorization for this entity is the FSC Electronic Payment Institution License, which is fully addressed in the step-by-step formation SOP and the Act Governing Electronic Payment Institutions.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable. The Taiwan Environmental Protection Administration has no EIA jurisdiction over a licensed electronic money institution.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt. No full EIA report and no environmental registration are required because the business generates no manufacturing or industrial effluent, no combustion emissions, and no hazardous waste streams.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable. There are no wastewater, VOC, or hazardous waste discharge thresholds triggered by virtual IBAN issuance or digital wallet reserve management; only ordinary office waste and municipal sanitary sewer obligations apply.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable at the industrial or civil-defense permit level. Standard office-occupancy fire-safety inspection, building occupancy certificate, and workplace safety compliance are required for the registered office, along with approved fire suppression and server-room fire protection for any data or racking areas. No industrial Civil Defense fire permit, structural load certificate, or chemical storage approval is applicable because no physical manufacturing, chemical processing, or warehouse operations are authorized under the FSC license.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry of Finance, Taiwan (Republic of China), acting through its regional National Taxation Bureaus; online tax services are delivered via the 'Ministry of Finance Tax Filing and Payment Service Network' (tax.nat.gov.tw) and the 'Integrated Service Platform for Electronic Invoices' (einvoice.nat.gov.tw).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: The Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture must first complete incorporation under the Company Act of Taiwan with the Ministry of Economic Affairs and obtain its company registration certificate. Step 2: No later than 15 days after the date of commencement of business, the company must file the statutory Business Tax Registration Application (Application for Establishment Registration as a Taxable Business Person) with the local National Taxation Bureau where the registered head office is located. Step 3: Supporting documentation must include the incorporation certificate, memorandum and articles of association, legal representative's identification, lease or ownership title of the Taiwan business premises, and the bank account opening certificate for the Taiwan operating account. Step 4: Upon successful verification, the National Taxation Bureau will issue a Tax Registration Certificate and assign the eight-digit Uniform Invoice Number as the statutory Tax Identification Number (TIN); the same number is used for Business Tax, profit-seeking enterprise income tax, and customs declarations. Step 5: The company must then register with the e-invoicing platform and apply for a Uniform Invoice issuance entitlement. Step 6: For the foreign non-resident parent or any non-resident service supplier with no Taiwan branch but deriving Taiwan-sourced taxable revenue, a separate Foreign Enterprise Tax Registration must be filed at the same Bureau, with an appointed Taiwan tax agent, a legalized/apostilled certificate of foreign registration, and a Taiwanese bank account for payment purposes; this non-resident TIN is used for reverse-charge Business Tax returns and withholding tax statements.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or hybrid mismatch election exists under Taiwan's Business Tax Act. Under the Income Tax Act, a domestic parent holding at least 25% of the voting shares of a Taiwanese subsidiary for 12 consecutive months may elect consolidated profit-seeking enterprise income tax filing; no other statutory tax classification elections apply.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Business Tax (VAT) - governed by the Value-Added and Non-Value-Added Business Tax Act of Taiwan
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No turnover threshold for registration; every enterprise engaged in Taiwan sales of goods or services must register before commencement. Monthly turnover above NT$200,000 in the prescribed preceding period triggers the mandatory issuance of Uniform Invoices and standard monthly VAT filing; turnover at or below NT$200,000 may be treated under the small-scale business taxpayer regime assessed at the special rate of 1% for goods sellers or 2% for service providers, as prescribed by the Ministry of Finance.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Taiwan statutory e-invoicing is mandatory for all Business Tax taxpayers liable to issue Uniform Invoices. The taxpayer must connect to the Ministry of Finance's 'Integrated Service Platform for Electronic Invoices' via the Uniform Invoice Turnkey API (the statutory XML/EDI interface) or, for over-the-counter retail activity, use the Cloud E-Invoice interface. Cloud e-invoices are cleared and timestamped in real time at issuance; B2B Turnkey invoices must be submitted within 48 hours of issue. The platform performs automatic line-item cross-checking with monthly VAT filings and applies a random-number anti-fraud stamp to each invoice. Failure to clear electronically renders the invoice invalid for input tax credit deduction and exposes the issuer to administrative penalties under the Business Tax Act.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Articles 7 and 8 of the Value-Added and Non-Value-Added Business Tax Act of Taiwan, 0% VAT applies to (i) physical export of goods with customs clearance, (ii) export services, including qualifying offshore digital services and fintech payment processing, supplied to foreign recipients where the service is performed outside Taiwan or is not used within Taiwan, (iii) sales to foreign embassies and consulates, and (iv) international transport. For an electronic money institution issuing virtual IBANs and managing digital wallet reserves, zero-rating is available only if the service recipient is a foreign enterprise or individual, the service is consumed outside Taiwan, the consideration is paid in a foreign currency from abroad, and the proceeds are repatriated to and settled in a Taiwanese bank account.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (electronic clearing-line record generated by the Taiwan Customs 'CPT Export Declaration System')
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill (negotiable transport document issued to the Taiwan exporter incorporating the export declaration number)
Commercial Invoice and Packing List (in English or bilingual; quantities, unit prices, ISIC/HS classification, and total amount must reconcile with the customs export declaration)

Foreign Exchange Settlement Certificate / Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) issued by an authorized foreign-exchange bank in Taiwan, evidencing that the export proceeds were received onshore within the prescribed repatriation window
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The National Taxation Bureau will audit zero-rating claims by matching the Customs Export Declaration, the bill of lading, the commercial invoice, and the bank's FIRC. If the foreign exchange is not received within the statutory 180-day deadline or the export justification fails, the claimed zero rate is reversed and the outstanding 5% Business Tax is assessed, plus late-payment interest. For fraudulent misrepresentations, Article 51 of the Business Tax Act imposes a fine of 5 to 15 times the evaded tax and may suspend the taxpayer's invoice-issuing rights; fabricating export documents can attract criminal liability under the Tax Collection Law and the Customs Anti-Smuggling Act. Assessments can be reopened within seven years where the statutory documentation bundle is incomplete or inconsistent.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of the Republic of China (Taiwan) (CBC), with the Financial Supervisory Commission (FSC) as the principal financial-sector and electronic-payment regulator. The Taiwan jurisdiction is treated separately from the Mainland China foreign-exchange regime; Mainland China SAFE rules apply only to a Mainland China entity, Mainland bank account, or Mainland transaction leg.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The New Taiwan dollar is generally convertible for bona fide current-account transactions, including trade payments, service fees, salaries, taxes, dividends, and other documented operating payments. Capital-account transactions, inward investment, outward investment, intercompany loans, guarantees, acquisitions, and repatriation of liquidation proceeds are subject to the Foreign Exchange Control Act, CBC reporting or approval requirements, bank documentary review, and applicable company-law or investment-review procedures. A foreign-invested Taiwan company may generally remit dividends after audited financial statements, shareholder approval, tax clearance or withholding compliance, and satisfaction of capital-maintenance and creditor-protection requirements. Principal and interest on approved or properly documented shareholder loans may be remitted subject to loan registration, tax withholding, transfer-pricing support, and bank review. There is no general prohibition on profit repatriation, but banks may delay or reject transfers lacking audited accounts, board or shareholder resolutions, tax evidence, beneficial-owner information, or a clear source-and-purpose trail. An electronic-payment or stored-value business may face additional safeguarding, segregation, customer-funds, liquidity, and regulatory-capital restrictions that limit the use of customer funds for dividend or treasury purposes.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Taiwan does not generally impose a universal mandatory surrender ratio or a fixed statutory conversion deadline requiring exporters to convert all export receipts into New Taiwan dollars. Export receipts may generally be retained in foreign-currency accounts or sold through authorized banks, subject to documentary evidence, transaction-purpose classification, anti-money-laundering review, and CBC reporting requirements. The exporter should retain customs declarations, invoices, bills of lading, contracts, collection records, and bank advices. Foreign-exchange settlement must be processed through authorized banks, and annual or transaction-based limits, declarations, or CBC approval may apply depending on the resident status, transaction type, cumulative amount, and whether the transaction is a capital-account item. A Taiwan company should not assume that export proceeds can be netted against imports, intercompany charges, or shareholder payments without bank confirmation and supporting documentation. If the relevant exporter is a Mainland China entity, PRC SAFE rules, including trade-receipt verification and any applicable conversion or repatriation requirements, must be assessed separately.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low to Medium for a licensed Taiwan operator and Low for an offshore digital EMI acting directly in Taiwan. Taiwan electronic payment institutions and electronic stored-value institutions must obtain the relevant FSC authorization and comply with the Electronic Payment Institutions Act, implementing regulations, AML and counter-terrorist-financing requirements, customer-fund safeguarding, operational-risk, information-security, outsourcing, reporting, and consumer-protection rules. A virtual IBAN or wallet product does not independently create a right to conduct Taiwan-regulated payment, stored-value, remittance, foreign-exchange, or deposit-taking activities. An offshore EMI may provide services only within the scope permitted by its home licence and Taiwan law; marketing to Taiwan residents, maintaining local customer balances, onboarding Taiwan merchants, or routing Taiwan payment flows may trigger Taiwan licensing, local-presence, agent, data, tax, and AML requirements. SEPA Credit Transfer is not a domestic Taiwan clearing rail and must be accessed through a correspondent bank or an appropriately licensed payment institution.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Taiwan law does not impose a universal rule that every director must attend a bank branch in person. Banks may permit remote or representative-led onboarding, particularly where the company, shareholders, directors, and beneficial owners have verifiable Taiwan documentation and an established banking relationship. In practice, a foreign-owned joint venture, high-risk electronic-payment business, complex ownership chain, offshore shareholder, virtual-asset exposure, non-standard payment flows, or expected high-volume foreign-exchange activity commonly triggers enhanced due diligence, video identification, notarized or apostilled documents, certified translations, an in-person meeting, local authorized representative attendance, or a branch interview. Remote onboarding is therefore a bank-discretion outcome, not an entitlement. The company should appoint a Taiwan-resident contact, maintain a registered office and operating substance, and pre-clear the account-opening package with the selected bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear legal authority to issue virtual IBANs, operate digital wallets, safeguard customer funds, provide remittance services, or conduct foreign exchange.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: FSC licence or written regulatory-status analysis; approved business scope; licensing application and correspondence; product flow diagrams; customer-funds safeguarding model; reserve and reconciliation policy; outsourcing register; AML and counter-terrorist-financing programme; sanctions-screening methodology; information-security controls; independent compliance officer appointment; and legal opinion identifying activities not requiring separate authorization.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque ownership involving Mainland China, nominee shareholders, trusts, layered offshore companies, or unidentified ultimate beneficial owners.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified constitutional documents for every ownership layer; shareholder register; group chart to natural-person beneficial owners; passports and proof of address; notarization or apostille where required; director and senior-manager identification; source-of-wealth statements; source-of-funds evidence; tax-residency declarations; sanctions and politically exposed person screening; and signed beneficial-owner certification.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital injection that does not match the registered capital, investment approval, shareholder resolution, or stated business plan.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Joint-venture agreement; articles of incorporation; foreign-investment approval or registration; capital subscription documents; board and shareholder resolutions; audited financial statements of the investor; bank statements; remittance advice; SWIFT message; investment-purpose declaration; capital-account filing or bank confirmation; and a reconciliation showing the relationship between subscribed capital and received funds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected payment activity resembles money transmission, payment aggregation, merchant acquiring, customer-wallet funding, or deposit taking without a clear regulatory perimeter.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: End-to-end funds-flow chart; contractual role matrix; customer and merchant terms; settlement timetable; safeguarding-account structure; transaction limits; reconciliation procedures; prohibited-use policy; chargeback and complaints framework; regulator correspondence; independent legal memorandum; and evidence that customer funds are not used for proprietary investment, lending, or dividend payments.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk countries, sanctioned counterparties, politically exposed persons, virtual assets, privacy-enhancing technologies, or unexplained rapid cross-border turnover.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Risk-based customer-acceptance policy; geographic-risk matrix; sanctions-screening vendor evidence; enhanced due-diligence files; transaction-monitoring scenarios; alert and escalation procedures; suspicious-transaction reporting protocol; counterparty onboarding standards; wallet or virtual-asset exposure controls; travel-rule assessment where relevant; and documented exit criteria.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between declared Taiwan activities and foreign exchange, SEPA, SWIFT, or correspondent-bank activity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Three-year business plan; expected transaction profile by currency, country, counterparty, and purpose; customer contracts; invoices; service agreements; merchant-acquiring agreements; customs records where applicable; pricing and fee schedule; tax registrations; staffing and premises evidence; and monthly treasury forecast approved by the board.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inadequate tax, accounting, or transfer-pricing support for intercompany fees, royalties, interest, dividends, or reserve-management services.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Intercompany agreements; arm's-length benchmarking; transfer-pricing report; withholding-tax analysis; invoices; tax residency certificates; beneficial-ownership evidence; board approvals; general-ledger mapping; audited financial statements; and evidence that regulated customer funds are excluded from group revenue and treasury pools.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Failure to demonstrate operational substance, local management, cybersecurity, business continuity, or segregation of duties.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Office lease; employee and payroll records; organization chart; responsible-officer appointments; internal-control matrix; SOC or penetration-testing reports; incident-response plan; business-continuity and disaster-recovery tests; vendor due diligence; access-control logs; dual-authorization policy; and internal-audit programme.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Use a regulated Taiwan bank and a dedicated capital-inward-remittance or foreign-investment account where required by the bank and investment authority. The remitter name must match the approved foreign shareholder or documented lender, and the payment reference should identify equity subscription, shareholder loan, or other legally permitted purpose. Before remittance, provide the bank with the joint-venture agreement, constitutional documents, investment approval or registration, capital subscription schedule, shareholder or board resolution, beneficial-owner information, source-of-funds evidence, and tax or regulatory filings. The bank should confirm the applicable CBC declaration, approval, annual settlement limit, and account designation before sending the wire. Use SWIFT MT103 or equivalent bank-to-bank payment instructions with complete ordering-customer, beneficiary, purpose, and intermediary-bank information. Do not route capital through an employee, customer-funds account, unrelated group company, personal account, or unlicensed payment intermediary. Reconcile the incoming amount to the capital ledger, issue or update the capital certificate, and preserve the SWIFT advice, bank credit notice, foreign-exchange declaration, and accounting entry. Shareholder loans require a separate loan agreement, arm's-length interest analysis, maturity and repayment terms, withholding-tax review, transfer-pricing support, and confirmation that the structure does not constitute unauthorized deposit taking or customer-fund financing.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For ordinary imports and cross-border services, use authorized-bank wire transfers supported by purchase orders, invoices, contracts, bills of lading, customs declarations, service acceptance records, and tax documents. SWIFT MT103 is appropriate for a direct customer payment; the bank may require correct purpose coding, ultimate-beneficiary details, sanctions screening, and evidence of the underlying transaction. Commercial letters of credit, documentary collections, open-account payments, and bank guarantees may be used according to counterparty risk and the bank's trade-finance policy. A commercial LC should specify the applicant, issuing bank, beneficiary, goods or services, currency, amount, Incoterms, shipment period, documentary conditions, discrepancy rules, and applicable ICC rules such as UCP 600 where agreed. Payments from regulated customer-fund or safeguarding accounts must be limited to permitted settlement, refund, and operational uses and must not fund unrelated group expenses, capital distributions, proprietary investments, or shareholder loans. SEPA payments require a European or other participating-bank correspondent and do not replace Taiwan foreign-exchange declarations, AML screening, or underlying-transaction documentation. Establish maker-checker approval, sanctions screening, beneficiary-account verification, payment-limit controls, duplicate-invoice detection, daily cash forecasting, and independent reconciliation.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable foreign-exchange forwards with an authorized Taiwan bank, limited to documented or reasonably forecast commercial exposures such as imports, exports, payroll, intercompany fees, debt service, and dividend payments; speculative trading should be prohibited by treasury policy.

Non-deliverable forwards may be available for currencies or markets where physical delivery is restricted, subject to bank eligibility, documented underlying exposure, applicable CBC and banking rules, counterparty limits, and confirmation that settlement does not evade capital controls or sanctions.

Currency swaps and cross-currency interest-rate swaps may be used for documented funding or currency-risk management through an authorized bank, with board-approved limits, ISDA or equivalent documentation, collateral and valuation procedures, accounting treatment, and related-party pricing support.

Foreign-exchange options or collars may be used where offered by an authorized bank and appropriate for a genuine exposure; premium, suitability, model-risk, early-termination, collateral, and accounting controls are required.

Hedging transactions should be centrally approved, linked to an exposure register, independently valued, periodically stress-tested, and reconciled to the general ledger. The company should not use customer safeguarded funds, regulatory reserves, or restricted capital for proprietary derivatives, and should retain confirmations, purpose declarations, valuation reports, and close-out documentation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual company status report and confirmation of registered particulars
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs or competent municipal government
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally May 1 to June 30 each year for the preceding year; confirm the applicable online filing window
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Company Act penalties generally apply for failure or inaccurate reporting, commonly TWD 10,000-50,000 and increased penalties for continued noncompliance; Taiwan does not generally impose automatic strike-off solely for late annual status reporting.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau of the Ministry of Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within five months after the end of the fiscal year; for a calendar-year taxpayer, generally by May 31
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or non-filing may trigger tax assessment, late-filing penalties, late-payment interest, and administrative fines under the Income Tax Act; persistent noncompliance may result in compulsory collection and other enforcement measures.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Audited annual financial statements and tax audit filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau; financial-sector filings also submitted to the Financial Supervisory Commission where required
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Submitted with the annual income tax return, generally within five months after fiscal year-end; regulated electronic payment institutions must observe additional FSC filing deadlines
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Tax penalties, reassessment, interest, and possible enforcement action; failure to comply with FSC reporting requirements may result in administrative fines, corrective orders, restrictions on business, or license-related sanctions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Electronic payment institution annual regulatory report and audited financial information
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Commission and other competent financial authorities, as applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally within the period prescribed for annual financial reporting, commonly within four months after fiscal year-end; exact deadlines depend on the institution's license and FSC instructions
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines, orders to rectify, enhanced supervision, business restrictions, responsible-person sanctions, and possible suspension or revocation of the payment institution license for serious or repeated breaches.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual shareholders' meeting approval of financial statements and profit allocation or loss offsetting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: No routine filing authority; corporate records retained at the registered office and provided to the competent authority upon request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Ordinarily within six months after fiscal year-end, unless a permitted extension or special rule applies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to prepare or approve statutory financial information may lead to Company Act penalties, director liability, tax-reporting deficiencies, and regulatory sanctions applicable to the licensed payment institution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial ownership, controlling-person, director, manager, and major shareholder information update
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs or competent company-registration authority; Financial Supervisory Commission and AML authorities where separately required
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally within 15 days after establishment or a reportable change; Taiwan does not generally require a standalone universal annual UBO confirmation for every company
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines, reporting orders, AML compliance measures, and possible regulatory action against the company and responsible persons for inaccurate, incomplete, or late information.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual labor insurance, health insurance, payroll withholding, and employment compliance reconciliation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau, Bureau of Labor Insurance, National Health Insurance Administration, and other competent authorities
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Periodic filings and payments apply throughout the year; annual reconciliation deadlines depend on the specific tax and insurance obligation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment surcharges, interest, administrative fines, assessment of unpaid contributions, compulsory collection, and potential employer sanctions.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A licensed electronic payment institution should be treated as subject to mandatory annual CPA audit and certification under applicable financial-sector regulations, irrespective of ordinary company-size thresholds. Ordinary Taiwan company thresholds may additionally require CPA tax-audit filing based on capital, revenue, employee count, public-company status, or other prescribed criteria.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Taiwan Financial Reporting Standards, which are substantially converged with IFRS; financial institutions and electronic payment institutions must follow FSC-prescribed financial reporting rules and industry-specific accounting requirements.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No general standalone annual UBO certification applies solely because a year has ended. The company must maintain accurate beneficial-owner and controlling-person records, report prescribed information on establishment and relevant changes within the applicable statutory period, and respond to AML, company-registration, tax, and FSC information requests. Share transfers must be documented in the share register and reflected in reportable ownership information when legally required.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors and Supervisors, if applicable
Audited financial statements and regulatory filing records
Electronic payment institution license and regulatory correspondence

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: Approximately USD 1,500-5,000 per year for a compliant Taiwan registered office and corporate secretarial service; licensed-financial-business support may cost more.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Approximately USD 15,000-60,000 per year for a regulated electronic payment institution, depending on transaction volume, internal controls, client-money or reserve arrangements, reporting complexity, and regulatory scope.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 20% corporate income tax on taxable income; an additional 5% tax applies to undistributed current-year earnings, subject to statutory exclusions and reinvestment rules.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Qualifying technology, innovation, biotechnology, strategic manufacturing, and other approved activities may obtain investment tax credits, R&D credits, accelerated depreciation, or statutory tax holidays. Eligibility is activity-specific and generally requires prior approval or compliance with prescribed investment, employment, technology, and filing conditions. A licensed electronic-money or digital-wallet business does not receive a general fintech corporate tax exemption solely because of its license.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax Return, including the annual income tax return and self-assessment schedules, filed through the Taiwan Ministry of Finance e-Filing and Tax Payment Service or approved tax software. The National Taxation Bureau having jurisdiction over the company's head office administers the filing.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; a provisional filing may be required for enterprises subject to Taiwan's provisional income tax filing rules.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a calendar-year company, the annual return and tax payment are generally due from 1 May through 31 May of the following year. For a non-calendar fiscal year, filing is generally due within five months after fiscal year-end. Provisional filing for a calendar-year company is generally due from 1 September through 30 September and is based on the preceding year's assessed tax or current-period computation, subject to statutory exemptions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Unified Business Number, legal name, registered address, tax authority, accounting period, filing type, and amendment or final-return status.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident shareholder or foreign group is not substituted for the Taiwan company as taxpayer. Report the Taiwan company using its own Unified Business Number and fiscal period.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net profit or loss under the company's approved financial accounts before Taiwan tax adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include only the Taiwan entity's accounts. Foreign head-office or shareholder accounting results must not be consolidated into the Taiwan company's return unless required under a specific statutory rule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deduct or separately identify statutory tax-exempt income, exempt securities income, qualifying investment income, and other legally excluded amounts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Do not treat foreign-source income as exempt merely because it is received through a foreign group account. Source, exemption, and foreign-tax-credit documentation must be retained.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add back income tax, penalties, unsupported expenses, excess entertainment expenses, disallowed donations, non-deductible provisions, excessive depreciation, and other book-tax differences.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Related-party management fees, service fees, royalties, financing costs, and shareholder charges require evidence of benefit, arm's-length pricing, withholding compliance, and business purpose.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report tax depreciation and amortization based on Taiwan statutory useful lives, approved methods, and asset classifications; reconcile book and tax amounts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign-group accounting policies do not determine Taiwan tax deductions. Taiwan tax rules and supporting fixed-asset records control.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclose material controlled transactions, transaction categories, counterparties, amounts, pricing methods, and any year-end true-up or tax adjustment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose cross-border payments to shareholders, parent companies, affiliates, and controlled treasury or technology entities. Maintain contemporaneous Taiwan transfer-pricing documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Claim eligible prior-year losses against current taxable income only where statutory bookkeeping, filing, and documentation conditions are satisfied.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A change in ownership, business cessation, merger, spin-off, or failure to file on time can restrict or eliminate loss utilization. Losses of foreign group companies are not deductible by the Taiwan subsidiary.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting profit or loss adjusted for statutory additions, deductions, exemptions, loss utilization, and approved incentives.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Taiwan entity must compute taxable income under Taiwan law even where consolidated group reporting uses another jurisdiction's accounting or tax basis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Apply the 20% corporate income tax rate to taxable income, subject to minimum tax, incentives, tax credits, and statutory alternative calculations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign tax credits are limited by statutory conditions and generally require foreign tax payment certificates, income allocation, and source documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculate alternative minimum tax where applicable, including qualifying exempt income and specified deductions under the Income Basic Tax Act.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Review minimum-tax exposure separately; a nominal corporate income tax exemption does not automatically eliminate minimum tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconcile Taiwan withholding tax suffered, withholding tax collected, tax payments, and refundable or creditable amounts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Taiwan company must withhold on applicable Taiwan-source payments to non-residents, including dividends, interest, royalties, and specified services, and must file separate withholding returns.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Determine the 5% additional tax on current-year earnings not distributed or otherwise qualifying for statutory exclusion or reinvestment treatment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Dividend declarations, capital reinvestment, and retained-earnings decisions must be reconciled with corporate approvals, accounting records, and shareholder withholding obligations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Submit the electronic return, financial statements, tax reconciliation schedules, shareholder and related-party disclosures, industry-specific schedules, and supporting certificates where required.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign-language documents may require Chinese translations, Taiwan authentication, notarization, or certified tax documents depending on the claimed deduction, exemption, or treaty position.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or non-filed annual returns may incur a penalty generally calculated by reference to tax payable, commonly 10% of tax payable subject to statutory minimum and maximum amounts; where no tax is payable, a fixed administrative penalty may apply. Failure to pay assessed tax may trigger statutory interest, collection surcharges, liens, seizure, and compulsory enforcement. False reporting, concealment, omitted income, or fraudulent tax evasion may result in additional penalties and criminal prosecution.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Provisional Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax Return, filed through the Taiwan Ministry of Finance e-Filing and Tax Payment Service where the taxpayer is not exempt from provisional filing.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Provisional semi-annual filing; not a quarterly corporate income tax return.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a calendar-year taxpayer, file and pay during 1 September through 30 September. The provisional amount is generally 50% of the preceding year's assessed corporate income tax, or an amount computed under the current-period statutory method where elected or required.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report the prior year's assessed corporate income tax used to compute the provisional payment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the Taiwan entity's assessed liability only; do not use the foreign parent group's consolidated tax liability.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Where the current-period method is used, report interim accounting income and statutory tax adjustments for the applicable period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply Taiwan tax adjustments and Taiwan-source rules to intercompany transactions occurring during the provisional period.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculate the provisional payment, apply permitted credits, and pay through an approved payment channel.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Payment of provisional tax does not replace the annual return, annual reconciliation, withholding filings, or transfer-pricing disclosures.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file or pay provisional tax may result in interest, collection enforcement, and administrative penalties under the Income Tax Act. The provisional payment is reconciled in the annual return and does not cap a later assessment.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Withholding Tax Statement and Withholding Tax Payment Filing, submitted through the Ministry of Finance electronic tax system and to the competent National Taxation Bureau.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Event-driven and periodic; withholding is generally paid by the statutory deadline following payment or accrual, with annual reporting requirements for withholding statements.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For payments to non-residents, withholding is generally paid within ten days after the withholding event, subject to the specific statutory payment rule. Annual withholding statements are generally issued and filed by the statutory January deadline following the calendar year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Recipient legal name, tax identification details, residence status, address, and beneficial-owner information.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Verify that the recipient is the beneficial owner and obtain a valid certificate of residence before applying treaty relief.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Classify dividends, interest, royalties, professional services, commissions, rentals, or other taxable Taiwan-source income and report the gross amount.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Do not recharacterize royalties, financing returns, or service fees as ordinary reimbursements without contemporaneous evidence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Apply the domestic rate unless a legally available treaty or cross-border agreement reduction has been properly established.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: China-Taiwan cross-strait tax treatment is not equivalent to a conventional comprehensive double-tax treaty. Do not apply a PRC treaty rate automatically to a Taiwan payment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report gross income, rate, tax withheld, payment date, and treasury remittance reference.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Taiwan payer remains responsible for under-withholding, late remittance, incorrect classification, and inaccurate reporting.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: The withholding agent may be assessed the unpaid tax, interest, and administrative penalties for failure to withhold, under-withholding, late remittance, or failure to issue and file required statements. Deliberate assistance in evasion may create criminal exposure.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 21% on dividends distributed by a Taiwan company to a non-resident individual or foreign enterprise, subject to applicable statutory relief. Dividends paid to Taiwan-resident shareholders are generally subject to domestic withholding or imputation rules according to shareholder status.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before payment, identify the recipient's tax residence, beneficial ownership, entitlement to relief, limitation provisions, and income classification. Obtain a valid certificate of tax residence issued or accepted by the recipient's residence jurisdiction, together with ownership, beneficial-owner, treaty-entitlement, and transaction documentation. Apply only the rate legally available under an effective agreement or Taiwan domestic exemption. Where advance approval, ruling, or competent-authority confirmation is required, obtain it before payment. Retain the certificate and supporting records and report the payment through Taiwan withholding filings. Taiwan and Mainland China do not operate a standard comprehensive income tax treaty providing an automatic reduced dividend rate; a PRC residence certificate alone does not establish a reduced Taiwan dividend withholding rate.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: The general Taiwan domestic withholding rate for royalties paid to a non-resident is 20%. The general rate for interest paid to a non-resident is 20%, although specific debt instruments, financial institutions, government bonds, securitized products, or approved financing arrangements may have special rates or exemptions. Treaty rates vary by agreement and commonly reduce interest or royalty withholding subject to beneficial ownership, residence certification, and procedural requirements. Payments for services performed in Taiwan, or other Taiwan-source income, may also be subject to 20% withholding unless a specific exemption or agreement applies.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File: generally required where the Taiwan enterprise's annual net operating revenue exceeds NT$300 million or its aggregate related-party transactions exceed NT$200 million, subject to statutory exemptions and transaction-category thresholds. Master File: generally required where the Taiwan enterprise belongs to a multinational enterprise group with annual consolidated revenue of at least NT$7 billion and the prescribed cross-border related-party conditions are met. Country-by-Country reporting may apply to groups meeting the applicable global revenue threshold, generally NT$27 billion or the prescribed equivalent threshold.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: Other methods permitted under Taiwan transfer-pricing regulations where the prescribed methods cannot reasonably be applied and the taxpayer demonstrates reliability and arm's-length results
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Taiwan has no separate UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations regime. Substance is nevertheless assessed under transfer-pricing rules, anti-avoidance principles, beneficial-ownership rules, controlled foreign company rules, thin-capitalization rules, withholding provisions, and the general anti-avoidance rule. The company should maintain Taiwan decision-making, licensed operational capability, personnel, premises, systems, risk control, capital, transaction records, and commercial rationale proportionate to its electronic-money and digital-wallet activities. A pass-through company with no real functions, risks, or control may lose deductions, treaty benefits, or the asserted characterization of payments.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Unlicensed electronic-money, payment, or stored-value activity
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Issuing electronic money, operating wallets, holding customer reserves, providing payment services, or accessing clearing rails without the required Taiwan Financial Supervisory Commission, central-bank, or other statutory authorization.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Regulatory orders, business suspension or revocation, disgorgement, administrative fines under applicable banking, electronic-payment, money-laundering-control, and financial-supervision laws, and possible criminal prosecution. Amounts depend on the violated statute and conduct.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and responsible officers may face personal criminal liability, administrative disqualification, civil restitution, asset preservation, travel restrictions where legally ordered, and imprisonment for intentional unauthorized financial activity or fraudulent conduct. Limited liability does not shield personal criminal acts.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax evasion and fraudulent tax reporting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Concealing revenue, fabricating invoices, understating Taiwan-source income, recording fictitious expenses, disguising distributions as loans, or submitting materially false corporate income tax or withholding returns.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Additional tax assessment, tax-evasion penalties, interest, compulsory collection, and criminal sanctions under the Income Tax Act. Serious intentional evasion can result in imprisonment and substantial criminal fines, with exact exposure depending on amount, method, repetition, and cooperation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Responsible directors, managers, accountants, and agents may be prosecuted personally, ordered to provide civil restitution, subjected to asset seizure and travel restrictions where authorized, and imprisoned. Corporate form does not protect persons who directed or knowingly facilitated evasion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends, interest, royalties, management fees, or Taiwan-performed service fees to non-residents without withholding, applying an unsupported treaty rate, or remitting withheld tax late.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recovery of the unpaid withholding tax from the withholding agent, interest, administrative penalties, statement-filing penalties, and potential criminal exposure for intentional fraudulent assistance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Responsible officers may face personal administrative or criminal exposure where they knowingly approved non-compliance; directors may also face shareholder or creditor claims for resulting tax liabilities.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using non-arm's-length prices, excessive related-party royalties or management fees, interest-free or underpriced financing, artificial year-end true-ups, or undocumented allocation of customer reserves and platform revenue.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax adjustment to arm's-length income, denial of deductions, additional corporate income tax, withholding-tax reassessment, interest, penalties, and possible minimum-tax consequences. Failure to provide documentation can permit a tax-authority determination based on available information.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers may incur civil liability for deliberate value extraction, breach of fiduciary duty, or fraudulent books, and criminal liability if the pricing was used to evade tax or transfer customer or corporate assets.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Routing Taiwan dividends, interest, or royalties through a conduit entity lacking commercial substance to obtain a reduced rate, or submitting an inaccurate residence certificate or beneficial-owner declaration.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty relief, withholding-tax reassessment, interest, penalties, information requests, and possible anti-avoidance or fraud proceedings.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Persons who knowingly arranged false treaty claims may face civil restitution, administrative sanctions, travel restrictions where authorized, and criminal prosecution for document fraud or tax evasion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Weak customer due diligence, anonymous or inadequately verified wallets, failure to identify beneficial owners, structuring transactions, failure to file suspicious activity reports, misuse of customer reserve accounts, or tipping off customers.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines, remediation orders, enhanced supervision, suspension or revocation of financial licenses, freezing or forfeiture measures, and criminal penalties under Taiwan anti-money-laundering and financial laws.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, compliance officers, and responsible managers may be individually liable for knowing, reckless, or negligent failures, including civil restitution, disqualification, travel restrictions where ordered, and imprisonment for laundering or intentional facilitation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Commingling customer funds with operating funds, using reserves for proprietary investment, creating unsupported reserve balances, failing reconciliation, or misrepresenting redemption capacity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Regulatory intervention, reserve restoration, restitution, fines, license suspension or revocation, civil damages, asset preservation, and criminal charges for breach of trust, fraud, or unlawful use of customer assets.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and senior officers may be personally liable for restitution and creditor or customer claims and may face criminal imprisonment where they knowingly misappropriated or authorized misuse of safeguarded funds.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: False books, invoices, or accounting records
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining parallel ledgers, fabricating vendor invoices, backdating intercompany agreements, omitting wallet liabilities, or manipulating reserve and revenue recognition.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax reassessment, accounting and corporate-law penalties, license consequences, civil damages, and criminal prosecution for false financial reporting, fraud, or document forgery.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, responsible accountants, and signatories may face personal civil liability, asset seizure, travel restrictions where authorized, and imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Illegal profit distribution or disguised repatriation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing capital or retained earnings without valid corporate approval, making shareholder loans from customer or corporate funds, paying fictitious service fees, or repatriating profits without required withholding.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Invalid-distribution recovery, withholding-tax and corporate-tax assessments, interest, penalties, creditor claims, and possible breach-of-trust or fraud prosecution.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors approving unlawful distributions may owe restitution to the company and creditors and may face disqualification, travel restrictions where ordered, and imprisonment for intentional misappropriation or fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to protect payment credentials, customer identification data, transaction logs, reserve records, or critical wallet infrastructure, or failure to report a material incident.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Regulatory fines, corrective orders, compensation claims, license restrictions, mandatory audits, and possible criminal penalties under financial, personal-data, and cybersecurity laws.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers may incur civil damages and regulatory sanctions for governance failures and may face criminal liability for intentional disclosure, concealment, or misuse of protected data.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Claiming that all platform, licensing, treasury, or service income is foreign-source while Taiwan personnel, servers, agents, management, or payment operations materially perform the business in Taiwan.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reclassification of income as Taiwan-source, corporate income tax and withholding-tax assessments, interest, penalties, denial of deductions, and possible permanent-establishment or tax-avoidance proceedings.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and tax officers may face personal exposure for knowingly approving false source allocations, including civil restitution and criminal tax-evasion liability where intent is proven.
